questions.question: At an intersection where all four corners have stop signs, who gets to go first?

options.text: The driver on your left.
The driver who arrived first.
The driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, drivers should go through in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Take a break every hour on long trips. Share driving with another person so you can both rest safely.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, which way should you steer?

options.text: To the right.
To the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the left.
questions.explanation: If you start to skid, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left to straighten out your vehicle.

questions.question: When there is a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, passing is allowed:

options.text: From the side with the solid yellow line.
From neither direction.
From the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: From the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When they are together, only drivers on the broken line side can pass.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and yield.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, look both ways, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look both ways, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean:

options.text: No one can pass.
Both directions can pass.
The right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: You should signal while turning because it:

options.text: Is required by law.
Tells other drivers and pedestrians what you plan to do.
Is always unsafe to turn off your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers and pedestrians what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians what you are about to do.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Watch what is happening in front, to the sides, and behind your vehicle at all times. This helps you see problems early and respond safely.

questions.question: On a road with multiple lanes, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: No one can pass.
Both directions can pass.
Only the direction next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the direction next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When a dashed line is next to a solid line, only drivers on the dashed line side can pass. Drivers on the solid line side cannot pass.

questions.question: Large trucks are most likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving in long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller cars. When going uphill, they lose speed easily. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull to the right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
Slow down and use high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: Before driving, clear snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows and mirrors. Clear all snow, ice, and frost from your vehicle before you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked stop line. Only go when it is safe. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which lane must you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning, use the lane closest to your direction of travel. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at a normal speed.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car skids.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast in wet weather causes your tires to lose contact with the road and ride on top of the water. This is called hydroplaning. Drive slower in rain than in dry conditions to prevent this.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road
Loose gravel
Slippery when wet

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: If you park uphill on a road with no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels to the right toward the edge of the road. This keeps your car from rolling onto the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: To help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
It is not safe to pass.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: "No passing zone" signs mean you cannot pass other vehicles in that area. These signs are used where it is unsafe to pass due to poor visibility.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to reach your destination faster.
Turn up the radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or need the radio loud to stay awake, you are too tired to drive safely. Find a safe parking spot and rest.

questions.question: How can you prevent yourself from becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Relax and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on driving. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Leave extra time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic exceeds the legal speed limit.

questions.question: You park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so the car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly frustrates other drivers and may cause them to make risky passing moves. Drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is crossing the street.
At all times.
Only when a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way at all times.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content and its effects on the body.

options.text: Caffeine
Fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have larger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have larger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the vehicle.
